item.title: API connections
item.description:
A connection and an endpoint are separate. One connection (base URL and auth) is reused by many endpoints.

@create api asks for the name, the base URL, and the auth. When Settings has environments or customers, the form asks for those too. A new connection starts on the header choice. Changing only the environment or the customer does not require another test after the current values have already passed.

Test connection sends GET to the base URL. Any HTTP status, including 401 or 404, enables Save. DNS failure, connection refused, timeout, or a failed token request does not.

item.title: Browse and edit
item.description:
Library on the rail, @library, or Cmd+Shift+L (Ctrl+Shift+L on Windows and Linux) lists everything saved: MCP servers, API connections, endpoints, OpenAI connections, SSH connections (Pro), and collections. SSH rows also have Connect.

Filter by name or by kind. The counts on the chips are what is on this machine.

item.title: Commands
item.description:
termorq-cli is a Pro-only companion tool. Its commands are listed here for Pro builds; the CLI has no edition switch. See the Free and Pro feature breakdown for app features.

@ opens the commands palette. Type to filter. Entries from commands.yaml follow these built-ins. @history is always available and is not a line in that file.

The shortcuts dialog lists the same triggers. The shot is the macOS wording.

item.title: Connections
item.description:
SSH connections are a Pro feature (ssh.connections in features.yml). Termorq speaks SSH itself, through the Rust russh library, so Windows does not need OpenSSH installed.

Create one link

@create ssh
@ssh new

Both open the same form.

Field What it takes
Name Unique, ignoring case. It becomes the tab title and the shell pill (SSH: prod-web)
Host A name or an IP address. Pasting deploy@10.0.0.5:2222 fills user, host, and port
Port 22 by default
User The account to log in as
Authentication Private key file, ssh-agent, or Password
Private key file OpenSSH or PEM key. ~/ is expanded. Browse… opens a file picker
Key passphrase / Password Stored in the OS keychain only. Blank on edit keeps the stored one. Forget the stored … clears it
Start in folder Optional. The shell starts with cd into it
Jump host Optional bastion: host, port, and user (blank uses the user above). The same authentication is used for both hops
Local port forwards Optional, one per line: 8080:localhost:80 or 5432:db.internal:5432. See sessions and files

Save keeps it. Save and connect also opens it in a new tab.

item.title: Install Termorq
item.description:
Termorq is a Windows desktop app available from the Microsoft Store. Use the badge to open the Store and install it.

After installation, open Termorq from the Windows Start menu. Microsoft Store delivers app updates for the Store edition.

Start using Termorq link

  • The window introduces the rail, prompt, tabs, and Settings.
  • Try the sample workspace to explore an example without connecting to a live API.
  • Browse the guide map to find the rest of the user guide.

Related pages link

  • The window

item.title: Model connections
item.description:
@create openai
@openai

@create openai asks for a name, a provider, an endpoint, a model or deployment, an API key, and an optional system prompt.

Provider What you fill in
Azure OpenAI The resource endpoint, the deployment name, and the key. This is the default. Existing connections stay Azure
OpenAI or compatible A base URL (blank means https://api.openai.com/v1), a model, and a key sent as a Bearer token. The key is optional for a local server

Ollama, LM Studio, vLLM, and a gateway work as the compatible base URL. Both Azure URL styles are accepted: an endpoint that contains /openai/v1, and a classic deployment host.

The keychain link

API keys, bearer tokens, basic passwords, client secrets, the OpenAI key, the MCP Azure client secret, and stdio env values whose names look like secrets use the OS keychain. The service name is com.garrardkitchen.ai-terminal.

item.title: Open, save, status, close
item.description:
Team workspace is a Pro feature. The @workspace commands are available in Pro builds; Free builds keep local definitions and collections.

A team workspace is a folder in a git checkout. The app reads and writes <folder>/.ai-terminal/ and never runs git commit or git push.

@workspace open ~/src/acme-apis
@workspace
@workspace status
@workspace save
@workspace close

@workspace with no verb is status. Settings → Team workspace → Open folder is the same open. workspace in the @ palette opens the same commands.

item.title: Preferences
item.description:
Open Settings from the left rail or select the avatar. The page groups preferences into Application, Workspace, Appearance, Terminal, and (in Pro) AI.

Application link

Primary email loads your Gravatar in place of the initials on the rail and in the header. The email is stored on this machine; initials stay if Gravatar has no photo.

item.title: Run a collection
item.description:
termorq-cli is available in Pro builds only. It runs saved collections without opening Termorq and provides commands for listing, checking, calling, and running them. The CLI has no edition flag or runtime switch.

termorq-cli runs a saved collection without opening Termorq. It uses the same HTTP calls, variables, response checks, and captures as the app. Version 0.25.0 prints termorq-cli 0.25.0.

The screenshots on this page are the real binary, taken against a sample workspace at /tmp/acme-apis. That workspace points Users API at mock://users, the app’s offline demo host, so nothing left the machine. A secret named in the prompt is shown as …. The value never appears in the output.

item.title: Servers
item.description:
@create mcp is one form and three transports.

Transport You provide
HTTP The endpoint. No credentials, or an optional OAuth client id for servers that do not register clients
Azure client credentials Tenant id, client id, client secret, scope
stdio Command, arguments, working directory, and env

When Settings has environments or customers, the form asks for those too. A new server starts on the header choice. Changing only the environment or the customer does not require another test after the current values have already passed.

item.description:
You type in one place. The first characters decide what runs. The accent caret follows the insertion point as you edit the line.

 shell["Shell"]:::out
 endpoint["@endpoint"]:::step

 line --> shell
 line --> endpoint

You type What runs
git status The tab’s shell. Output streams in. cd and export carry to the next line on bash, zsh, sh, and PowerShell
@endpoint List users A saved HTTP call
@tool search --query tea An MCP tool on a server connected to this tab
/explain how to make tea A skill from skills.yaml

@ opens the commands palette. / opens the skills palette. Both filter as you type. In the commands palette, exact and leading name matches appear before other name matches, and all name matches appear before description matches. Built-in @ actions are listed in Commands. Entries from commands.yaml follow them. @history is always first and is not a YAML entry.

item.title: The shelf
item.description: Collections are lines you already run: a shell line, an @endpoint call, or an @tool call. Collections on the rail, or Cmd+Shift+B (Ctrl+Shift+B on Windows and Linux), opens the shelf in the terminal column and hides the prompt. Press the shortcut again, or Esc, to return.

After each answer you see the tokens in and out and the chat’s running total. They are marked ≈ when the provider does not report usage. @chat on its own shows the total. @chat clear starts again.

item.title: Auth
item.description:
@create api offers seven auth kinds. The secret fields follow the kind. A blank secret on a later edit keeps the stored one.

Kind What you fill in Where the secret lives
None Base URL only Nowhere
API key Header name, default X-Api-Key, and the key Keychain, or a vault reference
Bearer The token Keychain, or a vault reference
Basic Username and password Password in the keychain, or a vault reference
Client credentials Azure tenant id, client id, client secret, scope Client secret in the keychain, or a vault reference
OAuth (browser) Authorization URL, token URL, client id, optional client secret Tokens in memory. Optional secret in the keychain
OAuth (device code) Token URL, device URL, client id, optional client secret Tokens in memory. Optional secret in the keychain

Client credentials are the Azure app-only flow: the app asks Entra for a token with the tenant, the client id, and the secret, then sends that token on the call.

item.title: Keyboard
item.description:
Cmd+/ on macOS, or Ctrl+/ on Windows and Linux, opens the shortcuts dialog. Press it again, or Esc, to close. The header hint (⌘/ help or Ctrl+/ help) opens the same dialog.

The labels below are the macOS ones from that dialog. Where a row says Cmd, Windows and Linux use Ctrl for that shortcut, except Ctrl+C, Ctrl+Tab, Ctrl+wheel, and Ctrl+0, which stay Ctrl on every platform. Ctrl+Shift+C copies inside the interactive terminal. On macOS the normal copy shortcut is Cmd+C.

item.title: OAuth sign-in
item.description:
An HTTP MCP server that answers 401 is ready for sign-in. You do not fix that in the create form.

@mcp signin Docs
@mcp signout Docs

@mcp signin <server> finds the authorization server from the WWW-Authenticate resource_metadata link (protected resource metadata, RFC 9728), and falls back to the well-known URLs. It then reads /.well-known/oauth-authorization-server (RFC 8414), then OpenID discovery.

item.title: Secrets and termorq-cli
item.description:
termorq-cli is a Pro-only command-line tool. It will not start a run that needs a secret it cannot find, and it scrubs every secret it does find from the text, JSON, YAML, and JUnit it writes. The app’s keychain, export files, and workspace guard get their own chapter later.

Where the secret comes from link

For each connection a step will call, termorq-cli looks in this order:

  1. The environment variable AIT_SECRET_<CONNECTION_NAME>.
  2. The connection’s vault reference, akv://… or op://….
  3. The app’s secret store, when that store can be reached on this machine.

The variable name is the connection name in upper case, with every other character written as _. Users API becomes AIT_SECRET_USERS_API. gh-prod.v2 becomes AIT_SECRET_GH_PROD_V2.

item.title: Sessions and files
item.description:
Open a session link

@ssh
@ssh prod-web

@ssh lists saved hosts with user@host, the authentication, and any jump host. Selecting one opens a new tab named after it. The shell pill in the status strip reads SSH: prod-web, and the terminal header shows SSH · connected.

The terminal is a full xterm: vim, top, tmux, and colours work. Ctrl+Shift+C copies and Ctrl+Shift+V pastes. exit or End session closes it and the tab goes back to the local prompt.

item.title: Share a file
item.description:
The Library import menu is the front door. Save dialogs start in Downloads. Files are written with owner-only permissions.

File Holds Secret
.aitcol Collections, and optionally the endpoints and API connections those lines use, plus chosen MCP servers A bundle that includes secrets is always encrypted. A plain collections file can be encrypted too. The preview flags lines that look like they contain secrets and can mask them
.aitmcp MCP servers only, including environment and customer ids Always encrypted. Password at least 12 characters, not stored
.aitapi The ticked endpoints and the API connections they use Encrypted, and the secret is inside. OpenAI connections stay behind. Password at least 12 characters, not a common password, not one character repeated
.aitbak Settings, environments, customers, theme, collections, MCP servers, API connections, endpoints, OpenAI connections, and SSH connections, including secrets Always encrypted

Older .aitmcp and .aitapi files still import. An older file may have no environment id or customer id. The names and colours stay in Settings on this computer.

item.title: Shells
item.description:
A line that is not an @ command or a / skill runs in the tab’s shell. One command runs at a time per tab. Output streams in while it runs. Ctrl+C stops that command and everything it started.

Which shells link

Settings → Shell picks the shell for every tab that has not chosen its own, from the ones installed here.

The rail is 64 pixels wide. Each button has a label and a tooltip.

item.title: Calling an endpoint
item.description:
@create endpoint asks for the connection, the name, the method, and the path. Methods are GET, POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE, HEAD, and OPTIONS. You can add query defaults, path parameters, and extra headers.

A {name} in the path becomes a path parameter with an optional default. Call it with --name value.

@create endpoint

Names may contain spaces. POST, PUT, and PATCH can include a JSON body, sent as application/json. A blank body sends none. The test shows the status as a coloured pill. Save stays disabled until an HTTP response comes back.

item.title: Files
item.description:
Two places hold state. The data folder is this machine. The workspace folder is what you commit.

Data folder link

com.garrardkitchen.ai-terminal under the platform data directory.

Platform Path
macOS ~/Library/Application Support/com.garrardkitchen.ai-terminal
Linux $XDG_DATA_HOME or ~/.local/share/com.garrardkitchen.ai-terminal
Windows %APPDATA%\com.garrardkitchen.ai-terminal
File What it is
collections.json The shelf. Older localStorage data is moved here once
command_history.json The last 500 commands and their times
api_connections.json API connections, without secret values
api_endpoints.json Endpoints
openai_connections.json Model connections, without the key
mcp_connections.json MCP servers, without secret values
ssh_connections.json SSH connections, without passwords or passphrases
ssh_known_hosts Host keys you trusted, in OpenSSH format. ~/.ssh/known_hosts is read, never written
mcp_prefs.json Favourites and related MCP preferences
network_settings.json The additional CA certificate setting

The keychain service is com.garrardkitchen.ai-terminal. An AES-256-GCM fallback file lives in this folder when the keychain cannot be used. Do not edit it to plant a token.

item.title: Free and Pro feature comparison
item.description:
Termorq has Free and Pro editions. This table shows which features each edition includes. The edition appears beside the application version in the window header; Free also shows created by Garrard Kitchen. Open License from the left rail to compare plans; the current build is highlighted.

The root features.yml manifest is the source of this feature list and the app’s feature availability. Every new feature must have an explicit plan assignment there.

item.title: Pipelines
item.description: termorq-cli is a Pro-only runner. A pipeline downloads the Pro CLI release asset for its runner, points it at the checkout with an absolute path, and passes each connection secret in from the forge’s secret store. The JUnit document is written to standard output. Warnings stay on standard error, so a skipped step does not corrupt the XML.

item.title: Sample workspace
item.description:
Download acme-apis.zip and unpack it. The workspace contains no token. Its Users API points to mock://users, an offline demo host, so calls stay on this machine.

Open it in Termorq link

Open Termorq and type the path to the unzipped folder:

@workspace open ~/Downloads/acme-apis

Change the path if you unpacked the sample somewhere else. The Users API connection needs a secret before it can run. For this offline example, any non-empty value works; it is not sent over the network. Enter it in the app so it stays in the OS keychain.

item.title: Tabs and splits
item.description:
Each tab is its own session: scrollback, folder, history, MCP servers, and OpenAI connection. Switching tabs leaves a running command where it is.

Add, rename, close link

+ adds a tab in the start folder. Right-click for Rename and Change colour. Middle-click, ×, or Close removes the tab. Closing the last tab resets it.

item.title: Tools, resources, and prompts
item.description:
@tool link

@tool
@tool search
@tool search --query tea
@tool echo --message hi
@tool echo --message=hi

@tool lists the tools on the servers connected to this tab, favourites first within each server, then A→Z. When more than one server is connected, the list names the server after the description. An empty @tool with an active connection shows Disconnect on the chip.

item.title: GraphQL and streams
item.description:
GraphQL link

Tick GraphQL on an endpoint. Its saved body is the query. The call sends POST with {"query", "variables"}.

The call’s body, or --body, is the variables JSON. A blank body sends {}.

A non-empty errors array shows as Check failed, so a check and a runbook treat it as a failure even when the HTTP status is 200.

item.title: Interactive terminal
item.description:
Most lines are non-interactive: the app starts the shell, streams the output, and returns to the prompt. A program that needs a keyboard opens a pseudo-terminal in the tab instead. On Windows that terminal is ConPTY. The screen is drawn with xterm.js.

These open a terminal on their own:

item.title: The inspector
item.description:
@mcp inspect Docs

Inspect on a row in @mcp opens the same dialog. The app connects that server on the current tab first if it needs to.

Section What you see
Overview Server info, instructions, the capabilities from initialize, and the negotiated protocol version
Tools Description, pretty-printed input schema, and annotations (read-only, destructive, idempotent, open world). Call… opens the usual tool form and approval flow
Resources Resources and templates (resources/list, resources/templates/list, following nextCursor). Read shows text, or the size and MIME type of binary contents. A template’s placeholders are filled first
Prompts Arguments, then Get shows the messages
JSON-RPC log The last 200 messages sent and received for that server. Memory only. Bodies over 16 KB are cut. Secret-looking fields and the server’s stored secrets are masked. Copy copies the log as text
Ping Sends ping and shows the round trip

A section the server has no capability for shows an empty state.

item.title: Web Check
item.description:
Web Check is a Pro feature, powered by the Pro-only termorq-cli. In the installed Windows app, open Termorq’s notification-area icon and choose Start Web Check. On macOS, use the menu-bar or Dock menu. Choose Show Web Check output to open the local URL and pairing code, then enter that code in the browser.

The tray menu has a Web Check submenu (Start Web Check, Show Web Check output, Stop Web Check, Open Web Check URL). On Windows and macOS a Copy submenu, after a divider, copies the URL, pairing code, data folder path, and source folder path. Open docs (help) opens this guide. On macOS click the Termorq icon in the menu bar to open the menu; on Windows right-click the notification-area icon. Open Web Check URL and Copy Web Check URL need Web Check running.

item.title: History and plain English
item.description:
Command history link

↑ and ↓ cycle the commands on this tab when no palette is open. The app keeps the last 500 in command_history.json in the app data folder. Each entry is the command and at, Unix epoch milliseconds. An older file that was a plain list of strings is migrated on load (at: 0 shows as an unknown time).

item.title: Import and export
item.description:
Two exports exist. One is a file another API client can open, with secrets replaced by placeholders. The other is an encrypted file for this app, and it can carry the secret.

OpenAPI and Postman, with no secrets link

In @endpoint, tick endpoints of one API connection and choose Export OpenAPI or Export Postman. Or type:

@export openapi Users API
@export postman Users API

That exports every endpoint on the connection.

item.title: Find and export
item.description:
Open links and files from output link

URLs and file paths in command output have a dotted underline. Ctrl+click (Cmd+click on macOS) opens a URL in the browser, or a file in its default app. Add Shift to show the file in Finder, Explorer, or the file manager instead. Relative paths such as src/App.tsx:12 are found from the tab’s folder, and ~/ is the home folder. A plain click still selects text. Only http and https links open.
